title: How do we change an age from days into other units?
description: One child is 4840 days old, another is 4070 days old, and a number with no unit might be an age. We change days into hours and minutes, days into years and days, and a million seconds into days. Keeko doubts the unit chosen for the large number.
teaching_notes: One idea: a smaller unit gives a bigger count, so estimate before deciding the unit. Watch for students who pick the unit for a large number without testing it.

source: Roxie is 4840 days old: find the age in hours, decide the unit of 6970710, find Estu's age in years for 4070 days, and a million seconds in days
video_script.why: Time units are changed by multiplying or dividing by how many small units make one big unit, and a smaller unit gives a bigger count.
video_script.substitution: Multiply to go to a smaller unit and divide to go to a bigger one, then test a large number against the age in days.
video_script.anchor: ages in days, a number with no unit, and a million seconds
video_script.wrong_answer: the number is the age in seconds
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that 6970710 is large and says it must be seconds. But 4840 days is 4840 × 86400 = 418176000 seconds, far bigger; the number fits minutes, since 4840 × 1440 is about 6969600.
video_script.payoff_line: A smaller unit gives a bigger count, so estimate before you decide the unit

final_answer.value: 116160 hours; 6970710 minutes; about 11 years and 52 days old; about 11.6 days
final_answer.spoken: The first child is one hundred sixteen thousand one hundred sixty hours old. The other number is the age in minutes. The second child is about eleven years and fifty two days old. A million seconds is about eleven point six days.

names.Laksh: the child who is 4070 days old
names.Ruhee: the child who is 4840 days old

maths_rules: 1 day = 24 × 60 = 1440 minutes: 4840 × 1440 = 6969600, close to 6970710, so the unit is minutes
in seconds the age would be 4840 × 86400 = 418176000, far bigger than 6970710
4070 days: 11 × 365 = 4015 and 4070 − 4015 = 55; about 3 leap days in 11 years give 55 − 3 = 52, so about 11 years and 52 days
video_script.design: A row of four small panels, one for each question, each showing a day and the unit it is changed into. The working area builds one conversion at a time.
open_questions: The 3 leap days in 11 years follow the worklist's 'about 52'; 4070 days is 11 years and 55 days without leap days.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='roxie'/>Ruhee is four thousand eight hundred forty days old.
<bookmark mark='hours'/>How many hours is that?
<bookmark mark='unit'/>The same age is also written as six million nine hundred seventy thousand seven hundred ten. In which unit is it?
<bookmark mark='estu'/>Laksh is four thousand seventy days old. How many years and days is that?
<bookmark mark='sec'/>And how many days is a million seconds?

beats.on_screen: the four questions stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 1 day = 24 hours; days to hours, × 24; hours to days, ÷ 24

marks.day: one day is shown as 24 small hour blocks
marks.mul: an arrow from days to hours is marked × 24

narration: <bookmark mark='day'/>One day has twenty four hours.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>To change days to hours, multiply by twenty four.
<bookmark mark='div'/>To go back from hours to days, divide by twenty four.

beats.on_screen: Given: 4840 days; 6970710 with no unit; 4070 days; 1000000 seconds

marks.given: the four facts are written in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two ages in days, the same age in an unknown unit, and a million seconds.

beats.on_screen: To find: hours; the unit of 6970710; years and days; days

marks.find: the four things to find are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to change the units, and decide which unit fits.
<bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, days to hours. Multiply four thousand eight hundred forty by twenty four.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Twenty times gives ninety six thousand eight hundred, and four times gives nineteen thousand three hundred sixty.

beats.on_screen: 1 day = 24 × 60 = 1440 minutes; 4840 × 1440 = 6969600, about 7 million, close to 6970710
narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, the unit. A day has one thousand four hundred forty minutes.
<bookmark mark='min'/>Four thousand eight hundred forty days make about seven million minutes.
That is close to the given number.

marks.leap: 55 − 3 for the leap days is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, years and days. Eleven years of three hundred sixty five days make four thousand fifteen days.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Four thousand seventy minus four thousand fifteen leaves fifty five days.
<bookmark mark='leap'/>Eleven years have about three leap days, so take away three.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, a million seconds. A day has twenty four times sixty times sixty seconds.
That is eighty six thousand four hundred.
<bookmark mark='mil'/>Divide one million by eighty six thousand four hundred.

beats.on_screen: 4840 days = 116160 hours; 6970710 minutes; about 11 years and 52 days; 1000000 s ≈ 11.57 days, about 11.6 days

marks.pay: the words smaller unit, bigger count appear

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>A smaller unit gives a bigger count, so estimate before you decide the unit.
<bookmark mark='ans1'/>Ruhee is one hundred sixteen thousand one hundred sixty hours old.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>That number is the age of Ruhee in minutes.
<bookmark mark='ans3'/>Laksh is about eleven years and fifty two days old.
<bookmark mark='ans4'/>A million seconds is about eleven point six days.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the number is the age in seconds, because it is so large.
<bookmark mark='secs'/>But four thousand eight hundred forty days in seconds is more than forty one crore.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is much bigger, so we test the unit before we decide.
